output.title: Check data residency before you automate
output.body:
Before you automate a workflow, make data residency the first control, not a footnote. Residency simply means where the data is allowed to live and move: on your own systems, in a specific country, or inside a vendor service. For an owner-operator, the useful question is not “can AI do this?” but “which parts of this workflow are allowed to leave my environment at all?”

Take one recurring workflow you already handle by hand, such as customer-data entry, invoice processing, or lead follow-up. Treat that as an example, not a customer case. Then list the fields you would not want to hand to a third party: payment details, personal data, internal pricing, or anything a supplier agreement keeps in place. The exact legal or contractual line is yours to check; Bareni does not make that call for you.

Next, read the tool’s own service terms and data-handling docs. If the platform cannot keep those fields where you need them, the workflow is not ready for that automation path, no matter how tidy the demo looks. If most of the workflow can move, a pilot may make sense. If everything must stay local, you are looking at a self-hosted or tightly integrated approach. Slightly less glamorous than a launch video, but more useful on Monday.
